t: You're looking at the bronze statue of Sir Robert Peel in Parliament Square, one of the first three statues placed in the square. It was sculpted by Matthew Noble, a leading portrait sculptor who also made monumental figures and busts of Victorian royalty and statesmen. Peel was Prime Minister, Chancellor of the Exchequer and Home Secretary, and one of the founders of the modern Conservative Party. He's regarded as the father of modern British policing, because as Home Secretary he founded the Metropolitan Police. That's the reason he stands so close to Parliament.
